paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God wants you to KNOW. Not hope, not guess, not cross your fingers behind your back. The writer says he wrote these things "so that you may know that you have eternal life" (1 John 5:13). That's a letter written to take the wobble out of your faith.

That knowing shows up everywhere in this passage. We can ask God with confidence, because "If we ask anything according to His will, He hears us" (1 John 5:14). When a brother stumbles, we ask God for him instead of just talking about him (1 John 5:16). And we know the One who was born of God protects those born of God (1 John 5:18). I bet that last one is the line I'd have wanted to hear back in the dark of that junk drawer.

The whole thing rests on one person: Jesus, who "is the true God and eternal life" (1 John 5:20). That's why the last line lands the way it does: "Little children, keep yourselves from idols" (1 John 5:21). Anything else that wants to be your foundation is a cookie cutter pretending to be the oven. So bake your day on what you KNOW, friend, and let Him be the One you lean on.
